newsitem.title: USA: FASB to delay date of provisions of Statement 125.
newsitem.headline: FASB to delay date of provisions of Statement 125.

text.p: The Financial Accounting Standards Board said Monday it proposed to delay by one year the effective date of certain provisions of Statement 125.
Statement 125 is now effective for transfers and servicing of financial assets and extinguishments of liabilities occurring after December 31.
The board said it will entertain comments from banks and other lending institutions on the proposal for 30 days.

The delay was sought by members of the broker/dealer community because the volume and variety of the transactions they engage in and the length of time it would take to get their information and accounting systems up to speed would make it difficult, if not impossible, to comply with Statement 125 as soon as January 1, a statement from the board said.
The one-year delay would apply to the provisions of Statement 125 that deal with secured borrowing and collateral, the statement said.
The statement also said it would apply to transfers of financial assets only for repurchase agreements, dollar rolls, and securities lending.
